title: Optimize CI hotpath: prune unused layers and unify warmup
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Background:
Our CI pipeline spends a disproportionate amount of time rebuilding image layers and re-running lint/toolchain installs on feature branches. This causes developer velocity regressions (slow PR feedback) and drives up runner time/cost. Previous efforts consolidated several base images but left divergent layer ordering across language runners and ad-hoc warmup scripts that are brittle.

Goal:
Reduce median PR build time for the most common fast-path (unit tests + lint) by 40% and reduce repeated install/cache churn across repository language runners. Provide a small, auditable set of warmup jobs and an explicit layer pruning process so images remain compact and cache-friendly.

Scope (this ticket):
- Harmonize Dockerfile base layer ordering across node/python/go runners so cache hits are maximized when shared deps or toolchain installs are stable.
- Introduce a deterministic layer-pruning job that removes stale intermediate layers from our internal registry (TTL-based) and rebuilds a curated set of seed images nightly.
- Replace per-repo random warmup shell scripts with a single centralized warmup pipeline (warmup:ci-hotpath) that primes the CAS and registry for expected commit ranges.
- Lift lint/toolchain install into a shared builder image (hermetic) and pin toolchain versions to a small manifest so full installs are avoided on PRs where possible.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the entire CAS architecture or introducing new storage backends (separate initiative).
- Major language runtime upgrades — we will pin minor versions and surface upgrade follow-ups.

Acceptance criteria:
- Median fast-path CI runtime reduced by >=40% on target repos measured over a 2-week window (compare baseline from 2026-02-01 to post-change).
- Nightly pruning job runs without errors for 7 consecutive days and reduces registry storage by at least 15% on test registry.
- Warmup job achieves >80% cache hit rate for the top 20 most frequent CI jobs within our ephemeral pool (Grafana dashboard shows metric).
- PRs demonstrate consistent lint/toolchain outputs (no regressions) and new builder image is published with signed manifest.

Implementation plan:
1) Audit current Dockerfiles across services and collect layer fingerprints + cache miss patterns (1 sprint, pairing with infra-observability).
2) Define canonical layer order for each language runner and author shared Dockerfile snippets stored in builders repo.
3) Implement nightly prune-and-seed job (k8s CronJob) with dry-run and canary for first 3 runs.
4) Build and publish hermetic builder images with pinned toolchain manifest; update CI to use builder image for lint/install steps.
5) Introduce warmup:ci-hotpath pipeline that uses historical commit ranges to prefetch artifacts into CAS and registry.
6) Monitor metrics (median CI time, cache-hit rate, registry size) and iterate.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature flagged changes to CI config to switch runners to new builder image for a subset of repositories (canary group).
- Observe for 48h, roll forward gradually to remaining repos.
- If regressions, rollback to previous builder and file a postmortem.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Centralizing toolchains reduces fragmentation but could slow adoption of necessary language upgrades; mitigated by short lifecycle for toolchain pins and explicit upgrade tickets.
- Pruning may accidentally remove layers still referenced by long-running build caches; mitigation: initial runs are dry-run, then move to TTL-based conservative pruning (e.g., 14 days).

Metrics to track:
- Median fast-path CI runtime (minutes) — primary success metric.
- Cache hit ratio per job (percent).
- Registry storage delta (GB) after pruning.
- Number of flaky CI failures introduced after builder switch (should be zero).
